Direct volume ray casting is an image-order rendering technique that casts a ray through a 3D volume for every pixel, sampling scalar values, mapping them to RGBA via a transfer function, and compositing samples front-to-back using alpha blending to produce the final image [S2, S3].

The claim accurately reflects the information provided in both sources. Source [S2] explicitly defines ray casting as an 'image-order direct volume rendering algorithm' where 'a ray is cast for each pixel into the volume,' involving sampling, mapping to optical properties (via transfer function), shading, and compositing. It also notes that front-to-back compositing is the most usual method. Source [S3] corroborates this by describing the process of casting rays from the virtual camera, interpolating values, and compositing the current value with the previously accumulated value (which implies front-to-back accumulation in this context). All specific details in the claim are present in the evidence.
